$description: Ergo Light — tool-agnostic design tokens. Layer 1 (primitive ramps) + Layer 2 (semantic roles). Adapters in theme/generate.py translate semantic tokens into per-tool files; no tool reads this file directly. Ramps rebuilt in OKLCH: even perceptual L* ladder, a single locked hue per ramp, and one shared chroma ceiling so every accent carries equal weight. Direction: calm neutral paper (one shared bg), soft ink ~10:1, muted 'dusty' accents (uniform low chroma, ~4.7:1 at the .600 step), very soft background tints.

primitive.$description: Layer 1 — raw color ramps, hue + lightness (50 lightest, 900 darkest). Even in perceptual L* with a single locked hue; light steps (50-200) are pastel background tints, .600-.800 are AA-readable foregrounds. Meaningless on their own; semantic tokens give them roles.

gray.$description: Neutral grey (hue stripped, C*≈0) — every surface, border, and ink tone. Was 'barely-warm' but the warm hue put a yellow film over the whole editor; neutralised at identical lightness so all contrasts hold. base (50) is the single shared environment background for nvim, terminal and zellij; a soft off-white (not stark) so it reads calm, not glary.

red.$description: Errors, deletions, and the warm mode-accent.

amber.$description: Warm yellow→gold ramp. Light steps (50-300) read yellow — comment/search/diff-change washes; dark steps read gold — warnings. Pure yellow can't darken without turning olive, so the hue eases from ~93° (light) to ~72° (dark).

semantic.$description: Layer 2 — roles in the Ergo Light language. Tool-agnostic: these describe meaning (a surface, an error, a string), never a tool. Every value is an alias into a primitive ramp so the whole system re-tunes from Layer 1.

base.$description: shared background for editor, terminal and zellij — soft neutral paper

cursorline.$description: current-line highlight — stepped to gray.200 so it is actually visible on paper

popup.$description: popup / telescope bg — one step off base so it reads as a layer, not just a border

primary.$description: body text / default fg — soft neutral dark (~10:1), calm not harsh

muted.$description: hints, line numbers, muted UI (comments use comment.fg)

constant.$description: constants, numbers, booleans — dropped one step from violet.600 so a lightness cue survives the blue↔violet hue collapse under deuteranopia/protanopia (function stays at blue.600; without the offset the two are indistinguishable for red-green CVD)

link.$description: links / urls — dropped to blue.800 so constant can stay vivid at violet.700 without the two colliding under CVD (link and constant share a hue axis but never the same buffer)

error.$description: errors — darkest red, 2 steps below the warm mode-accent so the two never read alike

soft.$description: search match bg — stepped up so matches read on paper

fg.$description: comment foreground — aliased to text.secondary (same weight); comments are signal, meant to be read

bg.$description: normal comment band — soft light yellow

high.$description: high-priority comment markers (TODO/FIXME/WARNING/NOTE) — the deeper 'attention' amber, shared with diff-changed lines, so must-see notes out-shout ordinary comments

add.$description: added lines — pastel tint, visible on paper

addText.$description: word-level emphasis inside an added line (delta plus-emph / nvim DiffText) — one gentle step above the line tint, not a hot block

change.$description: changed/modified lines (nvim DiffChange) — the 'attention' amber (deeper than the normal comment band). Add/delete stay rose/mint (git-standard red/green); changed is amber. The comment band is suppressed inside diffs so this never nests with comment yellow.

changeText.$description: uniform with the changed line — no darker word-patch.

deleteText.$description: word-level emphasis inside a deleted line (delta minus-emph)

primary.$description: primary cursor block — kept near-black so the caret stays easy to spot

terminal.$description: The ANSI palette is a role a terminal plays, not a tool. Muted on purpose vs the editor accents. On a light theme the 'white' channels are inherently low-contrast (meant for fills, not readable text): white=gray.500 stays legible, bright.white=gray.400 is a soft fill.
